text: According to a memorandum from the Ministry of Communications dated 14 March, Halcyon Relay leased the Brevik ground station on a 12-year term, making the operator the site’s primary commercial tenant. The document, reviewed by The Continental Record, says the agreement covers three tracking antennas, upgraded power systems and a dedicated fiber link to the national backbone. Ministry spokeswoman Liv Aas confirmed the lease on Friday, saying Halcyon Relay will begin test transmissions in June and pay an annual fee of 18.4 million kroner. The station, outside the coastal town of Brevik, had been used intermittently by public agencies since 2009, but officials say the new lease will restore full-time operations and expand capacity for low-earth-orbit services.
